A long-term investor, a swing trader, and a short-term trader should not manage risk the same way. They have different time horizons, different goals, and different reasons for owning a stock.

The easiest to manage risk is through position sizing.

A great company can still be a bad investment if the position is too large, bought too late, or held while the technicals are deteriorating.

And you don't have to sell everything just because it's below the 50-day moving average. You can sell in tranches: 1/3 when it breaks the 20-day moving average, another 1/3 below the 50-day moving average, and another 1/3 below the 200-day moving average (depending on your strategy.)

But just as importantly, you can buy it back if it starts to turn up again.

If the stock keeps working, you stay involved. If it starts breaking down, you reduce risk. And if it repairs itself and starts acting well again, you can rebuild the position.

You are simply adjusting exposure as the setup changes.

That is the whole point of risk management.
